lead.headline: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign mutual defense pact in Mecca
lead.dek: The Makkah agreement treats an attack on one as an attack on all.
body: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signed a trilateral defense treaty in Mecca on Friday, committing each state to treat an armed attack on any one of them as an attack on all three.

The joint statement says the accord is meant to strengthen collective deterrence and develop all aspects of defense cooperation. Saudi deputy minister Rayed Krimly said it is not an effort to build a military axis or a sectarian bloc, and is not tied to nuclear ambitions.

Saudi territory has been struck by Iran and Iran-backed forces in Yemen and Iraq since the United States and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28. Turkey fields NATO's second-largest military; Pakistan is the only Muslim-majority state with nuclear arms.

briefs.headline: Senate confirms Blanche as attorney general, 50-49
briefs.summary: The Senate voted early Saturday to confirm Todd Blanche, Trump's former personal lawyer, to lead the Justice Department. Two Republicans voted no.

briefs.headline: Employers cut 23,000 jobs in July as revisions deepen
briefs.summary: Payrolls fell 23,000 and May and June were revised down a combined 103,000. Unemployment was 4.1%; participation fell to 61.4%.

briefs.headline: ICE will release body camera video only in agency's interest
briefs.summary: A policy obtained by reporters lets the ICE director withhold shooting footage indefinitely. The agency bought $30.9M in cameras in July.

briefs.headline: Typhoon Dolphin batters Okinawa, closes eastern China ports
briefs.summary: Five people were hurt and 14,000 buildings lost power in Okinawa. Zhejiang halted 162 ferry routes before a landfall expected late Sunday.

briefs.headline: Colombia swears in de la Espriella on iron-fist platform
briefs.summary: Abelardo de la Espriella took office Friday in Cali after a narrow runoff win, pledging a hard line on drug traffickers.

briefs.headline: UN says Sudan's war has left 8 million children out of school
briefs.summary: Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed told the Security Council on Friday that five of six children in Darfur are out of school.

briefs.headline: FEMA clears Ritchie and Pleasants, denies Boone and Logan
briefs.summary: Gov. Patrick Morrisey said Friday the two counties won Individual Assistance for July's storms. Boone and Logan were denied for June flooding; the state may appeal.

briefs.headline: Nucor to close Apple Grove mill site Monday over threat
briefs.summary: A written threat naming Aug. 10 has the FBI, State Police and the Mason County sheriff investigating. About 500 employees work the site.

regional.item: A former Kanawha County deputy will stay in federal custody on sex crime charges after a magistrate denied release.

fishing.line: 96 cfs and falling - prime wading water.
Sound highs 4:22 a.m. and 5:07 p.m.; water 79.9F at Wrightsville Beach, 25 miles down the coast.

briefs.headline: Beilein headlines WVU Sports Hall of Fame class of seven
briefs.summary: The former men's basketball coach went 104-60 at WVU from 2003 to 2007. The class was named Friday and is inducted Oct. 10.

briefs.headline: Chelsea face AC Milan in Jakarta preseason friendly
briefs.summary: The club's fourth preseason fixture kicks off at Gelora Bung Karno Stadium, ahead of the Premier League season opening Aug. 21.

briefs.headline: UCLA steers heat through a crystal in focused rays
briefs.summary: Phonons moved through boron arsenide in ray-like patterns at room temperature, an effect previously seen only near absolute zero.

briefs.headline: Sunlight replaces the laser in entangled-photon experiment
briefs.summary: Ottawa and Max Planck researchers funneled concentrated sunlight into a crystal, producing photon pairs 94% faithful to an ideal state.

briefs.headline: Teen cannabis use tracks with slower cognitive gains
briefs.summary: A study following 11,036 children from ages 9 to 17 found users' memory and processing speed improved more slowly. THC drove it.
